purpose: Prevent geocentric/apparent-position and point-source shortcuts from being silently treated as validated lunar atmospheric-scattering geometry.

geometryBoundary.reasonRefractionDisabled: MYSTIC source rays in this contract are straight vacuum-to-atmosphere rays; using a refracted apparent Moon altitude would double-count or inconsistently introduce refraction that the radiative-transfer geometry does not model.

kiefferStone2005.title: The spectral irradiance of the moon
kiefferStone2005.relevance: ROLO image radiances are summed over the full lunar disk to form an irradiance-like quantity; the published operational model is disk-integrated irradiance rather than a resolved disk radiance distribution.

stoneKiefferBecker2003.title: Modeling the Radiance of the Moon for On-orbit Calibration
stoneKiefferBecker2003.relevance: USGS reported a spatially resolved ROLO radiance model, but described it as experimental, with simplified photometric functions and initial computational instabilities especially near the lunar poles.

usgsLunarCalibrationCurrent.relevance: USGS states that a spatially resolved radiance model exists but that disk-integrated irradiance is preferred because higher accuracy and precision are achievable.

usgsInstrumentTeamsCurrent.relevance: USGS states that its current instrument-team procedures pertain exclusively to disk-integrated lunar irradiance and that procedures for spatially resolved radiance comparison will be available once a reliable radiance model is operational.

satoEtAl2014LrocWac.title: Resolved Hapke parameter maps of the Moon
satoEtAl2014LrocWac.relevance: LROC WAC provides near-global spatially resolved Hapke photometric parameter maps at seven bands from 321 to 689 nm and 1-degree tiles; this is a research candidate for spatial weighting, not an admitted 380-780 nm absolute lunar radiance source.

preregisteredSensitivitySampling.sourceFluxAtEverySample: same full disk-integrated ROLO irradiance; each run is a hypothetical collimated unit-direction transfer response, not a partition of the lunar flux
preregisteredSensitivitySampling.diskTangentPlane: centered on frozen topocentric vacuum Moon-center direction
preregisteredSensitivitySampling.azimuthOriginDefinition: tangent direction from Moon center toward local zenith
preregisteredSensitivitySampling.azimuthPositiveDirection: toward increasing local astronomical azimuth; +90 deg is the tangent azimuthward direction
preregisteredSensitivitySampling.interpretation: This samples directional sensitivity across the physical lunar disk support. It does not by itself reconstruct the true resolved lunar disk, and finite sampling is not represented as a mathematical continuous-disk extremum proof.

transferKernelBound.definition: For fixed atmosphere, target direction and wavelength, define K(omega) as observer sky radiance per unit disk-integrated TOA lunar irradiance when the entire lunar irradiance is hypothetically placed in source direction omega.
transferKernelBound.sampledDiscreteSupportMeaning: For any nonnegative weights restricted to the frozen 33 sampled directions and summing to one, the weighted extended-source radiance lies exactly between the minimum and maximum sampled directional radiances.
transferKernelBound.reasonContinuousClaimRemainsClosed: Unsampled directions can in principle contain larger or smaller transfer response; no Lipschitz or monotonicity proof is frozen for K over the continuous lunar disk.
transferKernelBound.pointSourceApproximationReportingRule: Until a resolved disk integration is admitted, report the center-direction result together with the sampled directional envelope as an explicit finite-disk systematic sensitivity; do not collapse that envelope into observational fit residuals or tune it from X-Shooter.

resolvedDiskWeightingPath.goal: Convert the directional transfer kernel into a physical extended-disk integration while keeping the validated disk-integrated ROLO irradiance as the absolute source normalization.
resolvedDiskWeightingPath.historicalUsgsRoloResolvedRadianceReason: The 2003 USGS model was explicitly experimental and showed computational instabilities; current USGS instrument-team guidance says spatially resolved comparison procedures await a reliable operational radiance model.
resolvedDiskWeightingPath.lrocWacSato2014Coverage: seven WAC bands 321-689 nm; near-global 70S-70N; 1-degree Hapke parameter tiles
resolvedDiskWeightingPath.requiredNormalization: At each admitted wavelength and geometry, any qualified resolved nonnegative disk weights must be normalized to unit sum and multiplied by the frozen disk-integrated ROLO irradiance; no extra lunar scale factor is permitted.
resolvedDiskWeightingPath.fallbackIfResolvedModelUnavailable: retain center-source computational approximation plus explicit sampled finite-disk sensitivity; do not claim finite disk modeled
